echo_one.keywords: echo one delay echo slapback ping-pong tempo sync dotted eighth quarter repeats dub one knob
slider_desc: Delay amount in one move: 0 to 24 is a soft 1/16 slapback, 25 to 49 a 1/8 echo, 50 to 74 a dotted 1/8 and 75 to 100 a 1/4 note; feedback rises from 12% to 62%, the wet level to 50%, the ping-pong spread from 25 up, and the repeats get darker (low-pass 7 to 3 kHz). The time glides to each new value
uses: Tempo echoes on leads and synths
Ping-pong throws on the end of a phrase
Quick delay sketches with one control
echo_one.properties: Input → tempo-locked delay per channel (host tempo, 120 bpm without one; the time glides over 80 ms; up to 2 s) → low-pass and 150 Hz high-pass in the loop → feedback, crossing sides by the ping-pong amount → mixed with dry → Output. Zero latency.

warmer.keywords: warmer warmth warm tape tube saturation analog low mids soft top mix bus master one knob
slider_desc: Warmth in one move: 0 leaves the signal untouched; higher values drive the lows and low mids (below 600 Hz) into a gentle, slightly asymmetric tape/tube curve (drive x1 to x3, even harmonics) and lift them up to +2.3 dB, ease the top down by up to 2 dB and close a soft low-pass from 20 to 9 kHz, with a small trim so the level stays close to the input
uses: Warm up a thin vocal or acoustic guitar
Analog glue on the drum bus
A soft glow on the master
Take the edge off bright synths
warmer.properties: Input → split at 600 Hz (one pole) → lows: asymmetric tanh curve, DC removed, mixed in by Amount, +0 to +2.3 dB; highs: 0 to -2 dB → one-pole low-pass 20 to 9 kHz faded in by Amount → trim → Output. Zero latency.

closer.keywords: closer vocal voice presence proximity upfront forward compression dialogue podcast radio one knob
slider_desc: How far forward the voice comes: 0 is untouched; higher values raise the compressor's ratio (threshold -24 dBFS, up to 3:1, 5 ms attack, 120 ms release) and its make-up (up to +3 dB), a presence lift around 3.5 kHz (up to +5 dB) that eases off by up to half while the compressor works hard, and a proximity lift below 180 Hz (up to +2.5 dB)
uses: Bring a vocal to the front of a mix
Lift backing vocals or a choir
Acoustic guitar that needs to speak
closer.properties: Input → peak envelope of both channels (5 ms / 120 ms) → gain computer (-24 dBFS, 1:1 to 3:1) and make-up → + band-pass at 3.5 kHz (Q 0.9) scaled by the presence amount, reduced while the gain reduction reaches 6 dB → + one-pole low-pass at 180 Hz scaled by the proximity amount → Output. Zero latency.
